title: Assessment of Quinidine-Induced Torsades de Pointes Risks Using a Whole-Body Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Model Linked to Cardiac Ionic Current Inhibition.
authors: Zhang, Zexin; Zhou, Han; Yang, Yiting; Liu, Li; Liu, Xiaodong
one_liner_zh: 该文构建PBPK-PD模型评估奎尼丁致心律失常风险，核心为药物-离子通道作用，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合，与本课题无关。
abstract: The lethality of torsades de pointes (TdP) by drugs is one of main reasons that some drugs were withdrawn from the market. In order to assess drug-induced TdP risks, a model of cardiac ionic current suppression in human ventricular myocytes (ToR-ORd model), combined with the maximum effective free therapeutic plasma concentration or the maximum effective free therapeutic myocyte concentration was often used, with the latter proved to be more relevant and more accurate. We aimed to develop a whole-body physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) model, incorporated with a human cardiomyocyte pharmacodynamic (PD) model, to provide a comprehensive assessment of drug-induced TdP risks in normal and specific scenarios. Quinidine served as an example to validate the PBPK-PD model via predicting plasma quinidine concentrations and quinidine-induced changes in QT interval (DeltaQTc). The predicted plasma quinidine concentrations and DeltaQTc values following oral administration or intravenous administration of quinidine were comparable to clinic observations. Visual predictive checks showed that most of the observed plasma concentrations and DeltaQTc values fell within the 5th and 95th percentiles of simulations. The validated PBPK-PD model was further applied to assess the TdP risks using frequencies of early afterdepolarization and long-QT syndrome occurrence in 4 scenarios, such as therapeutic dose, supra-therapeutic dose, alkalosis, and hyperkalemia in 200 human subjects. In conclusion, the developed PBPK-PD model may be applied to predict the quinidine pharmacokinetics and quinidine-induced TdP risks in healthy subjects, but also simulate quinidine-induced TdP risks under disease conditions, such as hypokalemia and alkalosis.
abstract_zh: 药物引起的尖端扭转型室性心动过速（TdP）的致死性是某些药物退出市场的主要原因之一。为评估药物诱导的TdP风险，常采用人心室肌细胞中心脏离子电流抑制模型（ToR-ORd模型），并结合最大有效游离治疗血浆浓度或最大有效游离治疗心肌细胞浓度，后者被证明更具相关性和准确性。我们旨在开发一个全身生理药代动力学（PBPK）模型，并结合人心肌细胞药效学（PD）模型，以在正常和特定情境下全面评估药物诱导的TdP风险。以奎尼丁为例，通过预测血浆奎尼丁浓度及奎尼丁诱导的QT间期变化（DeltaQTc）来验证PBPK-PD模型。口服或静脉注射奎尼丁后预测的血浆奎尼丁浓度和DeltaQTc值与临床观察结果相当。视觉预测检查显示，大多数观察到的血浆浓度和DeltaQTc值落在模拟的第5和第95百分位数范围内。验证后的PBPK-PD模型进一步应用于评估TdP风险，使用200名受试者在4种情境下早期后除极和长QT综合征发生的频率，如治疗剂量、超治疗剂量、碱中毒和高钾血症。总之，所开发的PBPK-PD模型不仅可用于预测健康受试者中奎尼丁的药代动力学和奎尼丁诱导的TdP风险，还可模拟疾病条件下（如低钾血症和碱中毒）奎尼丁诱导的TdP风险。
